name: Ghostty
tagline: A fast terminal with a native interface on macOS and Linux
description: A terminal emulator that uses each platform's native interface toolkit and GPU rendering, aiming to be fast, standards-compliant and pleasant with no configuration at all.
backing: A non-profit project under fiscal sponsorship, started by Mitchell Hashimoto

maturity.rationale: Public since late 2024 and quickly adopted as a daily driver; its terminal-standards support is among the best. There is no official Windows build yet.

strengths: Native interface on each platform, so tabs, splits and windows behave like the rest of your system
Works well with zero configuration, and ships hundreds of themes
Excellent standards support, including the Kitty keyboard and graphics protocols
weaknesses: No official Windows version; only third-party forks
Configuration lives in a text file rather than a settings window

featureNotes.scriptable: Declarative config file and key-bound actions
